title: bonsai.run/1
description: The run report (contract §7.1): the log of one agent session on one task, opened at the start and appended to as it goes. A markdown file whose body is the workflow pack's template; this schema describes its YAML frontmatter as a reader returns it (JSON). Written by the agent that runs the session, on the builder's branch beside the code it describes; read by verifiers, the stop gate, Bonsai's tables and the studio. A writer writes every field below, in this order, null or [] where it does not apply (contract §2.2); a reader treats a missing field as null and keeps an unknown one. The frontmatter follows the format-1 YAML rules (contract §2.4).

format.description: The version line, always the first key (contract §2.2). In a file made from a template it carries a one-line pointer back as a trailing comment (contract §2.8).

id.description: R-<YYYY-MM-DD>-<task id>, with a suffix when a task has two run reports on one day (contract §7.1). The suffix's form is not fixed, so only the start is checked.

task.description: The task id this session worked on: the link between the two (the task carries no pointer back).

role.description: The role the agent ran as: a pack's role name.

model.description: The model the agent ran on, as the agent names it.

started.description: When the session started, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM as text (contract §2.4), or null.

finished.description: When the session finished, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM as text, or null while it runs.

outcome.description: How the session ended, a closed list (contract §7.1). A format-0 report keeps its words: needs-rohan reads as needs-person, needs-review as needs-verifier, anything else as other.

commits.description: The commit hashes this session made, each quoted in the YAML (a bare hash can read as a number); [] when none. Contract §7.1 fixes no length, so none is checked.

labels.description: A map of label name to value (contract §5), for example a cost a program outside agent sessions writes; {} when none. Names are <namespace>.<name> with one dot.
